text:
michael_cs: Heads-up — new customer Nimbus hitting a reproducible pattern during sandbox ramp: we see tokens minted, then an immediate 401 for the first request, followed by a flurry of 429s across their websocket fanout. Any ideas?
jia_engineer: heres a sanitized seq: POST /session/create -> 200 {token: "tk_abc", ttl: 20}
WS OPEN (handshake) -> 200
WS MESSAGE -> 401 {err: "invalid"}
HTTP /v1/embeds -> 429 x 18
We spawn a pool of 80 thin worker shards that each do a WS handshake with a token at startup.
rory_sre: curious: are you exchanging that token for connection-scoped credentials or reusing the same token string for every shard?
jia_engineer: reusing the same token string as issued; we pass it in the WS auth query param and also in Authorization header for HTTP calls.
auth-bot: quick note: our platform treats short-lived session tokens as bound to the issuing handshake ID. If the same token is presented from multiple concurrent shards it can trigger our duplicate-detect and revoke flow in some edge cases. That would explain immediate 401s. The 429s look like hitting the burst window from many simultaneous first requests.
michael_cs: so two problems: token binding + warmup fanout. Any mitigation we can apply today?
rory_sre: yes. Two options: 1) short-term: enable token delegation on your auth proxy — exchange one master token for per-shard delegated tokens (one call to /session/delegate that returns N short-lived non-replayable tokens); 2) alternative short-term: serialize WS handshakes with jitter and use a single coordinator process to distribute tokens to shards. Both reduce duplicate-use revokes and spread initial requests.
jia_engineer: how would delegation look?
rory_sre: pseudo flow: POST /session/delegate {count: 80} -> 200 {tokens: [t1,t2,...]} Each delegate token is bound-once and safe to use concurrently without tripping our duplicate-protection. We can enable delegation for your tenant for 48h if you want to test.
michael_cs: can we also bump their burst allowance while they ramp?
quota-manager: @michael_cs applied tenant "nimbus" temporary burst +5rps for 48 hours (chg: U-33911).
jia_engineer: that would be helpful. Any client-side flags we should try in parallel?
rory_sre: yes — three small changes: add tokenLeewayMs=5000, set wsHandshakeSerialLimit=5 (max concurrent handshakes), and enable connectionResetOnRotate=false (we keep connections but rotate per-shard token header). Example config snippet: ```js
client.opts = { tokenLeewayMs: 5000, wsHandshakeSerialLimit: 5, handshakeJitterMs: 150 };
```
auth-bot: also instrument: add X-Shard-ID and X-Delegation-Id headers on handshakes so server logs can attribute duplicate presents. We'll surface those in traces for the next 24h for tenant nimbus.
jia_engineer: tried coordinator-based distribution + jitter and reduced concurrency; immediate 401s disappeared within 2 mins and 429s dropped to background noise. Delegation enablement would be nice long-term.
michael_cs: great. I'll capture these steps in the onboarding playbook entry "delegated tokens + warmup patterns" and flag the account as "ramping - low risk" for renewals.
rory_sre: follow-up infra task: add an explicit response header when duplicate-token detection happens (x-token-dup: 1) to make debugging clearer. I'll file infra/ISSUE-1282.
jia_engineer: thanks all. We'll share a short note on how our auth proxy can request delegations. Happy to join a quick sync tomorrow to flip delegation on.
michael_cs: perfect — thanks team :raised_hands:
